title: From the Desk of the CEO: Trayd Accounting is Here
summary: Trayd Accounting is here: general ledger, AP/AR, financial statements and job costing built on your payroll and field data. A note from CEO Anna Berger.
body_markdown:
Every dollar in construction starts in the field, but for decades, the systems running construction have treated the field and finance like two separate worlds.


The crew knows the hours and materials used. The foreman knows the schedule. Someone captured all of it, on the job, the day it happened.


But the finance team finds out weeks later—from a payroll report, invoices trickling in, or someone else’s memory of what happened on site.


That’s not self-service. It’s a bottleneck. And the industry has been paying for it for over forty years.


We’re done waiting.


**Today, we’re launching Trayd Accounting.**


A platform built around the job, not the ledger. Because when financials start at the job, everything downstream is connected.


The crew clocks out, and the cost hits the job. The PM sees the budget update live, with access to exactly what they need. Invoices are parsed by AI as they come in, costs are connected back to the job, and everything flows into WIP, AIA billing and the P&L—every number traceable back to its source.


For years, contractors have tried to close this gap by stacking point solutions around systems like Foundation, Sage 300 and QuickBooks.


More software never created more visibility. It just created more places for the truth to live.


Trayd Accounting changes that.


One construction-native operating system, built on a single source of truth.


Sam Ostrow at Ostrow Electric ran the same on-premise system for 27 years before making the move. Once he saw payroll, job costs and accounting working together, “the value became obvious.”


Lendyn Prickel at Prickel Electric put it plainly: QuickBooks always had the team making decisions based on numbers that were already two weeks stale.


That’s exactly what we set out to change.


Trayd Accounting is live for contractors across the U.S. today. And we’ve priced it around the same belief we built it around: financial visibility shouldn’t be rationed by seat.


This one is special.


It’s the piece that makes Trayd whole: the field, payroll, and now the books, one platform all the way through.


Accounting was the hardest mile to get right. The team worked meticulously, and I couldn’t be prouder of what we shipped.


For too long, construction’s financial truth has lived in a vault only one or two people could open. We believe the people running the job should have access to the information they need, when they need it.


The PM sees what the PM needs. The office sees what the office needs. Leadership decides who sees what.


That’s visibility.


And visibility is what lets contractors make decisions sooner, operate smarter and grow with control.


**Trayd is visibility. Visibility is scale. Scale is growth.**


Come see what field to finance actually looks like.


**Field to finance, finally.**
